fields.summary: Technical spike - TinyMCE RTL menu navigation keyboard behavior

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Task

components.name: Text editor TinyMCE
components.description: The default text editor in Moodle 4.2 onwards

fields.description:
While investigating [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|smart-link], we discovered that TinyMCE's keyboard navigation in dropdown menus with submenus does not behave correctly in RTL (Right-to-Left) mode. In RTL languages, pressing the Left Arrow key should open submenus (moving right in RTL context), and Right Arrow should close them. Currently, the behavior remains in LTR mode regardless of the directionality configuration.

After peer review discussions, we determined this is an upstream TinyMCE issue rather than a Moodle-specific problem. The TinyMCE menu navigation logic uses hardcoded LTR arrow key handling and does not expose a supported API to override these keybindings for RTL mode.

An initial workaround was implemented using keyboard event interception to swap left/right arrow keyCodes in submenu contexts. However, this approach is fragile, depends on internal TinyMCE DOM structures, and would likely break on future TinyMCE upgrades while potentially interfering with built-in accessibility behavior.

The purpose of this technical spike is to:

# Report the issue to the TinyMCE team via GitHub (completed)
# Monitor and track the upstream response and any potential fixes
# Document the investigation findings and recommend next steps based on TinyMCE's response

Links:

* Original Moodle issue: [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|smart-link]
* TinyMCE GitHub issue: [https://github.com/tinymce/tinymce/issues/10757|https://github.com/tinymce/tinymce/issues/10757|smart-link]  
* Test fiddle: [https://fiddle.tiny.cloud/UxJHSuv2tx/0|https://fiddle.tiny.cloud/UxJHSuv2tx/0|smart-link]

fields.description:
*Description:* When a user attempts to upload a file with a filename exceeding 255 characters, the operation fails due to the {{VARCHAR(255)}} constraint on the {{filename}} column in the {{mdl_files}} table.

Screenshot below per XMLDB in moodle sandbox

!Screenshot 2025-12-17 at 12.21.46 pm.png|width=671,alt="Screenshot 2025-12-17 at 12.21.46 pm.png"!

Currently, this results in a database write error rather than a user-friendly validation message. Furthermore, when testing with extremely long filenames (e.g., >500 characters), the resulting error message in the Boost theme renders incorrectly, causing text to overflow bounds and become illegible.

*Technical Context:* The {{mdl_files}} table schema restricts filenames to 255 characters.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Create a dummy file on your local machine with a filename longer than 255 characters (e.g., 300+ characters). If you hit a character limit on your local system, continue anyway.
# Log in to Moodle.
# Navigate to any activity that accepts file uploads (e.g., Assignment, File Resource, or Private Files).
# Attempt to upload the file via drag-and-drop or the file picker.
Where you’re prompted for the file name in the picker, make the text larger than 255 characters (I just typed garbled words and copy pasted)

*Actual Result:* The upload fails, triggering a database exception regarding the {{VARCHAR}} constraint. The user interface may display a generic error or, in cases of very long filenames, a broken UI element where the error text overflows the container (specifically observed in the Boost theme).


!image-20251217-015628.png|width=671,alt="image-20251217-015628.png"!

*Expected / Suggested Behavior:* The system should handle long filenames in one of the following ways:

# *Schema Update:* Increase the {{VARCHAR}} constraint in {{mdl_files}} to accommodate longer filenames.
# *Auto-Truncate:* Automatically shorten the filename to fit within the 255-character limit (preserving the file extension) and notify the user.
# *Theme fix:* If the {{VARCHAR}} constraint in {{mdl_files}} should not be changed, make corrections to theme so that the error message displays correctly. Truncating the file path in the error, or not displaying it at all if that makes things appear better.

fields.description:
When you set up Oauth2 authentication for users already created with other auth types, an email is sent to confirm the linked login, and if the users clicks on the link inside that email in a 30 minute period the linked login becomes established.

[https://docs.moodle.org/n/OAuth_2_authentication|https://docs.moodle.org/n/OAuth_2_authentication]

[https://docs.moodle.org/en/Linked_logins|https://docs.moodle.org/en/Linked_logins]

The issue happens when that 30 minute period expires and the user haven’t confirmed the linked login; in that case if the user tries to login via OAuth2 again Moodle throws an error message (_This account is pending email confirmation._) and therefore the user cannot start the process again and gets locked.

I’ve seen that this requests are stored in mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login, so I’ve been able to clean up the expired tokens executing this query:

{noformat}delete from mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login aall
 where(   aall.confirmtokenexpires<>0
      and to_timestamp(aall.confirmtokenexpires)< CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '30' MINUTE
      );{noformat}

but I’d say:

* There should be a place inside Moodle to remove expired requests (both as a users and as an admin)

and/or

* There should be an scheduled task that removes all the expired requests

fields.summary: TypeError when trying to use \core\route\require_login for courseless login checks

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
I’m trying to implement a controller for a non-course-centric route, using the following attribute helper:

{noformat}...
requirelogin: new require_login(
    requirelogin: true,
    autologinguest: false,
)
...{noformat}

This is synonymous with the old require_login(null, false); login is required, but not for a course.

Currently, the above results in a TypeError because moodle_authentication_middleware calls $requirements->get_course_attribute_name(), which is typed to return a string (but actually is a nullable param underneath). If we’re not setting that param in the attribute declaration, then it’s null and results in that TyepError. Additionally, in the middleware, $courseorid is conditionally set, only if we’re able to get this courseattributename. 

I think we want to support null in the login helper -  i.e. make get_course_attribute_name() return null or string - and then support null as a valid value for $courseorid in the middleware, so we can then pass this along to require_login() there too. It seems this was the intention of this code, as there’s already calls to require_login there - hence reporting this as a bug for now.

resolution.name: Fixed

fields.description:
This is only a problem in a site that IS NOT configured with routing. At the time of writing this, that’s the default.

To reproduce:

# Go to course/tags.php?id=<courseid> or course/admin.php?courseid=<courseid>
# Notice you get an “unusual” error reported.


In 4.5, these pages worked, and in 5.0+ they still work in the UI, because we’ve fixed the navigation to use r.php/course/<courseid>tags (and the same for course/admin, presumably, though I didn’t check that one). 

I was just under the impression that these existing files should continue working as they did in 4.5, without the need to prefix the path with r.php. If that’s incorrect, then feel free to close this issue.
